picks.title: [Bible] Episode 336: Pete Enns - Pete Ruins Everything on Lamentations
picks.summary: In this week’s episode of The Bible for Normal People, Pete explores the book of Lamentations and what it can teach us about faith in the midst of suffering. He examines the book’s historical setting in the aftermath of Jerusalem’s destruction, its raw and unsettling portrayals of grief, anger, and God’s apparent absence, and the ways its carefully structured poetry gives shape to experiences of trauma and loss. He also considers how Lamentations challenges modern Christian assumptions that faith requires certainty, optimism, or resolution. Together, these themes invite listeners to see lament
picks.reason: Explores Lamentations' honest portrayal of suffering and faith amid trauma.

picks.title: Why Are There Four Gospels?

picks.title: Was Paul an Eyewitness of Jesus' Resurrection?
picks.summary: In a recent response to Wes Huff, Bart said the only eyewitness we know of who's converting people is Paul. A lot of people pointed out that Paul never met Jesus. Fair. But Paul is also the only person in the New Testament who tells us, in his own words, that he saw Jesus alive after his death. Everyone else reaches us secondhand. Bart unpacks what Paul actually claims to have seen, why Paul is the only person who claims to see a resurrected Jesus, and why the earliest firsthand evidence for the resurrection suggests visions.
picks.reason: Bart Ehrman discusses Paul's eyewitness claim of the resurrected Jesus and its implications.
